llm.summary: The macro vice tightened again overnight: Treasury yields at 24-year highs, Waller explicitly signalling further hikes while naming AI capex as an inflation source, oil jumping on tanker attacks in/near Hormuz and a drone strike on a UAE nuclear plant, and 30-year mortgages at 7.5% with buyer demand collapsing. The new and most important datapoint is not macro but micro: the Nvidia-backed Firmus IPO closed books with cratering demand at a $30bn ask, and SpaceX's $40bn chip-financing bonds printed record-wide CDS. That is the first visible rejection by public capital markets of the leveraged leg of the AI build — the equity-funded core (NVDA, MSFT, TSMC beating September sales) is still accelerating, but the credit-funded periphery is being repriced. Simultaneously Microsoft and Nvidia launched RTX Spark laptops, Surface Ultra and Dell agentic workstations, pushing inference to the device and opening a real PC refresh cycle into a DRAM cost squeeze. Power remains the least-contested claim on AI: Google took 890MW from Constellation, Meta is funding seven gas plants, and CEG/EQT/VST sit at 94 attention with pricing at 58/39/48 — attention without price. Flows are still a one-sector market (Technology +80, every other sector negative, Real Estate -89, Financials -80), which means there is no second leg if Tech wobbles. The regime model keeps draining from both clean outcomes into Stagflation (+5) and Reflation (+5). For the book, DXCM and BAX sit in the worst flow sector, SMCI/HPQ are levered to memory pricing and to a long end moving the wrong way, and CRM is the cleanest agentic-AI exposure trading at a de-rated multiple.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: risk-off skew inside a tape that refuses to break, because the only sector attracting flow is the one being repriced by yields. Oil above the reflation threshold plus a Fed openly contemplating more hikes means the discount rate and the input cost rise together — the classic squeeze on long-duration equity. The Firmus IPO failure is the tell to trade: public markets will fund compute earnings but not compute promises. Expect dispersion inside AI — profitable toll-takers (NVDA, TSMC, MSFT, ASML) hold, while levered neoclouds, pre-revenue AI IPOs and anything financing GPUs with debt widen. Gold stabilising off a two-month low rather than extending suggests the move was real-yield mechanics, not liquidation; it stays capped while the dollar firms. Every rate-sensitive consumer series (housing at 7.5% mortgages, beer, big-ticket, new autos) keeps degrading irrespective of the index level, and PEP's cut forecast plus STZ's guidance slide confirm mid-tier consumer demand is genuinely soft, not rotationally soft.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: the defining structural change is that AI capex has migrated from cash flow to credit, exactly as the Fed turns hawkish partly because of that capex. That is a reflexive loop with one weak link — residual value on depreciating silicon pledged into debt structures. It argues for owning utilisation (chips, networking, semicap, foundry) and electrons over the entities doing the borrowing. Power is the most contracted earnings stream on the tape and sits in the most hated flow buckets: Google/Constellation, Meta's gas plants, ASEAN load growth of 5.4% annually, nuclear PPAs proliferating — against Utilities flows at -74. That gap closes. Edge AI becomes a real 2027 hardware cycle as Windows agentic PCs ship, but the margin accrues unevenly because DRAM/NAND pricing is being bid away by data centres. Macro stays reflationary-with-sticky-prices: tariffs now identified by the NY Fed as the entire cause of everyday-goods inflation, Hormuz risk premium in crude, fiscal supply keeping term premium elevated. Housing stays frozen; value retail and off-price keep taking share from aspirational brands.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: three lines. First, compute and generation are a single capital decision — an advertising company funding gas plants and a search company signing multi-gigawatt nuclear says the scarce input is firm power, not models. Generation, the fuel cycle, grid equipment, HVAC and cooling get revalued from flow-depressed levels. Second, agents become the interface and the metering layer; whoever owns identity, delegation, payment rails and runtime containment collects a per-action toll, which is why Cybersecurity tops the flow ranking and why agentic software platforms with installed distribution (CRM, MSFT) matter more than model labs. Third, the cost of capital has structurally reset: a long end at 24-year highs with permanent term premium means chronic housing undersupply because nothing pencils at 7.5%, a decade in which equities must clear a real bond hurdle, and a durable premium on hard assets with contracted cash flows over levered duration and asset gatherers.

short_term: Housing demand is being withdrawn rather than deferred: at 7.5% mortgage rates, buyers pull back, lock volumes fall, and households redirect the shelter budget into rent, maintenance and staying put — directly feeding storage, home improvement and repair spend over transaction-linked spend.

Consumers are trading down and trading out of discretionary categories entirely: PepsiCo cutting its forecast, Constellation Brands struggling to bring beer drinkers back, Levi's guidance slide — the mid-tier is being hollowed while value retail and essentials hold.

Investors are abandoning narrative-only risk: Bitcoin ETF outflows as yields rise, bitcoin to $82k, Firmus IPO books closing short. Cash yielding 5%+ at the long end is now a genuine competitor to speculative equity, and capital is demanding contracted cash flow.

Households are feeling energy as a bill, not a chart: rising electricity-bill search queries and winter heating cost anxiety convert the oil/power story into a direct, salient squeeze on discretionary income.

Firms are shifting AI spend from experimentation to procurement of agents that replace workflow cost — Dell/Microsoft/Nvidia shipping agentic PCs and workstations means the buying decision moves from the CIO's pilot budget to the IT refresh line item.

Attention is rotating to defense and drones (attention 84, +54% vs 28d) and to stablecoins (83, +46%) — the public is pricing conflict and monetary workarounds simultaneously, a classic late-cycle security-plus-hedge posture.
long_term: Security is displacing convenience as the organising consumer and corporate need: energy security, supply-chain security (critical minerals, COSCO blocked in Germany), space-based defense, counter-drone, and digital identity for agents.

Productivity is being purchased rather than hired: agentic software and on-device inference let firms buy throughput per dollar instead of headcount, which structurally compresses white-collar hiring and raises the return on software and silicon relative to labour.

Time and cognitive bandwidth become the premium goods: agents that transact, negotiate and schedule on a user's behalf shift the consumer relationship from browsing to delegation, which erodes the advertising-attention model and creates a new per-action payment layer.

Electricity becomes a household-salient cost and a national-strategic good simultaneously, normalising nuclear in places that resisted it (Bangladesh starting generation, Slovakia, marine reactors) and making on-site generation a corporate procurement competence.

Shelter aspiration mutates: a generation priced out at 7.5% rates reallocates toward mobility, experiences and portable status goods rather than ownership, deepening the rental/build-to-rent structural bid and the undersupply.

Health is shifting from episodic treatment to continuous monitoring and metabolic management, but the funding environment for it is now rate-sensitive — adoption continues while the equity multiples compress.

portfolio_implications.why: Two live risks converge: memory/component cost inflation compressing already-thin server margins, and the Firmus IPO failure plus record SpaceX CDS signalling that the credit-funded buyers who absorb SMCI's rack capacity face a closing funding window. Revenue acceleration and a below-history valuation justify keeping a position, but 5% is too large into a tape where AI financing is the specific thing being repriced. Cut toward 3%.

The Microsoft/Nvidia/Dell agentic PC launch validates the refresh-cycle thesis that underpins the position — but it also shows the premium tier being attacked by Microsoft directly and by Dell's workstation push. HPQ captures volume, not mix, and DRAM pricing is being bid away by data centres. Hold on the FCF and valuation case; do not add until memory pricing stabilises.

The cleanest holding in the book relative to today's tape: agentic AI shipping into Windows and enterprise workflows is exactly the theme exposure flagged as strengthening, Technology flows are +80, and the multiple sits below its own history. It is capital-light productivity — it wins from AI without borrowing to buy GPUs, which is the distinction the market is now making.

Physical AI (AWS machine tooling, NVIDIA factory digital twins) is a genuine multi-year tailwind and the fundamentals are improving, but Industrials flows at -58 and HRI's -7.7% gap on equipment rental say the real-economy capex cycle is softening at 24-year-high yields. Hold, do not add until Industrials flows turn.

Health Care flows at -48 with no improvement, the name already gapped down, and nothing in today's tape gives the sector a bid. The operating fundamentals are intact — margins, ROIC and FCF all expanding — but this is dead money while the long end rises. Reduce to a half position and reclaim the risk budget for contracted-power or defense exposure.

Cheap on both absolute and relative measures with revenue accelerating, but it combines the worst sector flow (-48) with rate-sensitive leverage into a 24-year-high long end. Needs an explicit catalyst — a guidance reset or balance-sheet action — or it should be sold to fund exposure where attention exceeds pricing (CEG, EQT, PGR, defense).

what_changed_since_yesterday: The AI funding story moved from anecdote to evidence: Firmus closed its IPO books with cratering demand at $30bn — Bloomberg explicitly framing it as a warning on AI funding. Yesterday the leverage concern was theoretical; today a deal failed.

Waller added a new transmission channel by naming AI spending as a driver of cost pressure while signalling further hikes. AI capex is no longer just a discount-rate victim; it is now cited as a cause of the discount rate.

Energy security escalated from shipping lanes to generation: a drone attack on a UAE nuclear plant alongside tanker attacks and slowing Hormuz flows, plus Pentagon strike preparation and Trump saying he does not want an Iran deal.
Gold stopped falling — recovering from a two-month low as the dollar rally stalls — which supports the read that the break was real-yield mechanics rather than the start of a hard-asset unwind.

Microsoft and Nvidia executed a coordinated edge-AI platform launch (RTX Spark laptops, Surface Ultra, revamped Windows 11, Dell creator PCs and workstations). This is the first concrete 2027 PC refresh catalyst and directly reframes HPQ's competitive position.
Mortgage rates ticked to 7.5%, the highest in nearly three years, with demand visibly withdrawing — housing is now the clearest real-economy casualty.

The consumer cracked more publicly: PepsiCo cut its earnings forecast, Levi's guided down, Constellation Brands conceded beer demand remains a problem. Yesterday this was a rotation debate; today it reads as fundamental.
The regime mix kept draining from both clean outcomes — Goldilocks -4.5 and Contraction -5.5 into Stagflation +5 and Reflation +5 — with Contraction still the single highest probability at 28.2.
